BINDING CORRECTION 1 (no verdict shopping): two records for the same split entry REFUSE at finalize with a typed code; the caller must never be able to run a child twice and keep the better verdict. The repair names the existing next-round route; it is a refusal of this merge, not a dead end. BINDING CORRECTION 2: a stray record whose entry id is not in the split, or a record that cannot be attributed to an entry, also refuses. (4) RECEIPT: the optional `splitSha256`; a receipt without it verifies exactly as today. (5) WHOLE CHAIN (PO rule: a fix is the whole chain, never one step): one regression walk with the real commands and real state, not stubs of the steps under test: preflight prints the split, admit, N child verdict stops through the real hook entry, merge, finalize, the receipt verifies, and `close-coordinator` assertCriticIndependenceForClose accepts the label with no PO acknowledgement; first read whether guard-dispatch or the packet binding allows several Critic children under one admitted packet and fix or STOP accordingly. Restate in place with a G20-72 comment the w277 case `actual direct CLI preserves complete packet-ready` so it also strips `split` (QG-04: never weaken another assertion). Regression cases: above the bound one entry per module with disjoint scopes covering every changed path; below the bound no split field; each merge refusal; a split packet with one child missing, with two records for one entry, with a stray entry, and with a merged verdict differing by one finding each refuse at finalize; a non-split packet behaves byte-identically.
